cs.t: > I would happily use the phone I had 10 years ago > There is no such thing on the market now Good news, the ~12-year-old BlackBerry Q20 is back, and shipping, [0] with an updated motherboard. It's a real product, not vaporware; I have two. It has a headphone jack, a small form-factor, removable micro-SD card slot, and a battery that takes little more than a guitar pick and #0 Philips screwdriver to replace. Parts are cheap as hell as well, with a new screen costing under $25USD, and replacement keyboards under $30. There's multiple clean sheet designs [1,2] of similar devices as well. Though I expect them to be treated like fun little runabout cars: made for (typically young) people that can't justify the cost, leaving nobody to buy them, who then bemoan their discontinuation... due to poor sales [0]  https://zinwa.com/product/q25-full-device/  [1]  https://zinwa.com/product/p26-full-device-pre-order/  [2]  https://www.clicksphone.com/ca/communicator

cs.t: I was involved in porting some software to Qt back when Photon was deprecated, and I always found the system very interesting. This is the first time I'm actually learning more about its history. Thanks for the great read. I was also a huge fan of BlackBerry phones (having used Q5 and Z10 as daily drivers). The system was solid and had some really cool ideas. Too bad it didn't work out...
